newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate softens in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate softens in liquid market.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates slipped on Tuesday as the market remained awash with cash, traders said.
The average interbank call loan rate slid to 11.0625 percent from the previous 11.09375, with the Central Bank maintained its overnight rates.
"There's so much money in the system, with most banks offering money to the Central Bank," said one trader.
Traders said they expect banks to swamp a government auction later today of two-year bonds due to excess funds.

"I expect the yield on the two-year bonds to drop to 13.75 percent from the previous 14 percent in line with the drop in the August inflation and the corresponding fall in the Central Bank's rates on Monday," said one trader.
Some 25.96 billion pesos changed hands among 35 lenders and 20 borrowers.
Secondary trading on government securities was moderate with the yield on the 91-day treasury bill pegged at 11.7 percent.
Six months bills were quoted at 11.7 percent and one-year bills at 12.5 percent.
